title: Choosing Photography and Imagery for Your Brand: How to Keep Pictures Consistent and Safe to Use

cards.heading: Give each image type a job
cards.text: Photos, stock and illustration can mix, if each has a clear job.

cards.heading: Describe your style briefly
cards.text: Pick subject, mood, light and composition, then test five images together.

cards.heading: Check the licence first
cards.text: Easy to find does not mean free to use. Confirm terms in writing.

cards.heading: Keep a simple image record
cards.text: Note the source, licence terms and date for every picture you use.

cards.heading: Test pictures at the smallest size
cards.text: Check they stay clear as thumbnails, and that any text on top is readable.

facebook.message:
Does your website look like it was put together by three different businesses?
Mismatched photos are one of the quickest ways to weaken a good brand. Our latest guide covers how to describe a consistent image style, what to check before you use a picture, and what to tell a designer.
Swipe through for the key points on choosing and checking brand imagery.

To read the full article, visit the FinTaxTech website and find "Choosing Photography and Imagery for Your Brand: How to Keep Pictures Consistent and Safe to Use" in our Blog section.
